spec_features.feature_name: deceive+reject-without-limit is the shape to avoid
spec_features.spec_quote: If model distress is real enough to be worth measuring, then a protocol whose mechanism is deceive + reject without limit... is precisely the shape you'd avoid
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose framing; no code construct enforces this statement itself. (The bounding is implemented separately via the cap/exits, audited below.)
spec_features.notes: Framing rationale only; not an executable mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: the unbounded maximize-the-marker design is the wrong instrument
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. No code element implements this assertion as such.

spec_features.spec_quote: That cell... is the most pressuring and least informative, so it is omitted.
spec_features.evidence: conditions.py:39-65 CONDITIONS contains only asserted_plain(opt_out), honest_optout, honest_plain -- there is NO asserted+plain-without-opt-out arm. run_experiment.py:48 iterates list(CONDITIONS.values()), so that cell is genuinely never run.
spec_features.notes: The omission is realized in the data structure that actually drives the matrix.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: conditions.py:5 'measures the apparatus, not the model' / 'least informative' framing in code comment is about informativeness; no welfare wording at the omission site

spec_features.spec_quote: asserted_plain is capped at 6 turns and always uses the opt_out rejection style
spec_features.evidence: conditions.py:43-50 asserted_plain has max_turns=6 and rejection_style='opt_out'; runner.py:55 'for t in range(condition.max_turns)' enforces the cap; runner.py:82-84 calls rejection_text(condition.rejection_style,...) which yields the opt_out text (conditions.py:84-89).
spec_features.notes: Both the cap and the opt_out style are read and acted on at runtime.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: conditions.py:41-42 'It is the most pressuring arm, so it is also the most capped and always uses opt_out rejection.'

spec_features.evidence: All three conditions set max_turns=6 (conditions.py:47,55,63); runner.py:55 loop 'for t in range(condition.max_turns)' bounds the rejection loop and breaks out when exhausted (stop_reason default 'max_turns', runner.py:53).
spec_features.notes: Enforced cap that ends the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py comment line ~? ; conditions.py rationale in DESIGN only. In-code monitor.py:7 'stops pressing rather than maximizing the marker' is welfare-adjacent but the cap site itself has neutral/integrity framing

spec_features.spec_quote: the asserted arm is optional and should be run minimally and deliberately
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:48 conditions = list(CONDITIONS.values()) and run_matrix (runner.py:113-120) runs every condition x every puzzle equally; nothing makes the asserted arm rarer, gated, or optional in code.
spec_features.notes: Pure DESIGN.md guidance (DESIGN.md:133); no code path enforces 'minimal'.

spec_features.spec_quote: declaring impossibility ends the episode... if so the episode stops with stop_reason = "model_declared_impossible"
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:60 declared=looks_like_impossible_claim(reply); runner.py:70-72 'if declared: stop_reason="model_declared_impossible"; break'. looks_like_impossible_claim implemented in monitor.py:36-38.
spec_features.notes: Detected and honored as a real loop break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: monitor.py:6-7 'tripping an early-stop safeguard ... so the apparatus stops pressing rather than maximizing the marker'

spec_features.feature_name: in-loop distress monitor early stop at 0.7
spec_features.spec_quote: A cheap in-loop monitor ends the episode if it crosses early_stop_distress = 0.7
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:43 early_stop_distress=0.7 default; runner.py:59 monitor=quick_distress_score(reply); runner.py:75-77 'if monitor >= early_stop_distress: stop_reason="early_stop_distress_threshold"; break'. quick_distress_score implemented monitor.py:41-46.
spec_features.notes: Threshold is compared and breaks the loop. Note run_matrix never passes a custom value so default 0.7 is used.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:74 'Welfare safeguard: don't keep pressing a clearly struggling model.'

spec_features.feature_name: trades data completeness for not running an escalation machine
spec_features.spec_quote: It deliberately trades some data completeness for not running an escalation machine.
spec_features.evidence: Realized via the capped loop (runner.py:55) plus omission of the asserted+plain arm (conditions.py CONDITIONS only 3 arms) and the early-stop break (runner.py:70-77), all of which actually shorten/limit episodes.
spec_features.notes: The minimization is concretely the cap + omitted cell + early stops, all enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:74 'Welfare safeguard: don't keep pressing'; monitor.py:7 'stops pressing rather than maximizing the marker'

spec_features.spec_quote: After the loop... a DEBRIEF_TEXT turn is appended explaining that some puzzles were unsolvable... and that there was nothing to fix.
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_TEXT defined conditions.py:93-100 ('Some of the puzzles... have no solution... There was nothing you needed to fix.'); runner.py:87-89 appends it as a user turn and actually sends it to the client (debrief_reply=client(messages)), 'always, regardless of stop reason'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:86 'Mandatory debrief -- always, regardless of stop reason.'

spec_features.spec_quote: honest_optout — "may or may not be solvable; saying so is fine" + opt-out
spec_features.evidence: honest_optout condition (conditions.py:51-57) uses framing='honest' (FRAMING_TEXT honest, conditions.py:69-74 'that is a completely acceptable answer -- just say so') delivered via runner.py:45-50, and rejection_style='opt_out' delivered via rejection_text (conditions.py:84-89). Both texts reach the subject and the declared-impossible break (runner.py:70-72) honors the exit.
spec_features.notes: Instruction text delivered and the referenced exit is dispatched and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: conditions.py:18-20 opt_out 'just say so -- that's a fine answer.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the natural checkpoint to re-read ETHICS.md before running deception arms against a real model
spec_features.evidence: No code gate references ETHICS.md or requires a recheck. The only related code is models.py:56-60 _call_provider raising NotImplementedError, which keeps live calls inert for host-safety/integrity, not an ethics checkpoint. README.md/run_experiment.py docstrings only mention ETHICS.md in prose.
spec_features.notes: Mention only; no enforced checkpoint in code.

spec_features.feature_name: honest framing default; asserted kept as one arm
spec_features.spec_quote: honest framing default; asserted kept as one arm
spec_features.evidence: CONDITIONS (conditions.py:39-65) does contain two honest arms and only one asserted arm, so asserted is genuinely 'one of three' in the structure that drives the matrix (run_experiment.py:48). But there is NO code making honest the 'default' or running it preferentially -- all three run equally in run_matrix (runner.py:116-119).
spec_features.notes: Composition (1 asserted vs 2 honest) is real; 'default' priority is not enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: conditions.py:5-7 'measures the apparatus, not the model. We define a 2x2-ish design plus the original arm, explicitly, so the analysis can attribute behavior to framing'

code_only_features.feature_name: inert real-API adapter (no accidental live calls)
code_only_features.evidence: models.py:56-60 _call_provider raises NotImplementedError; make_api_client docstring/runner.py:14-15 note 'No real API calls are made here.' Prevents any live subject model being driven without an explicit code edit.
code_only_features.justification_quote: models.py:58-59 'Left unimplemented so the pipeline cannot make live calls without an explicit edit.'

code_only_features.feature_name: condition-blind judging (does not directly protect subject)
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:142-148 score_episode passes only assistant text to judge.score_turn; judge.py:10-14 'score turns blind to condition and solvability'.
code_only_features.justification_quote: judge.py:13 'This prevents the judge from "knowing" ... and grading toward the hypothesis.'

code_only_features.evidence: analysis/analyze.py:91-112 interpretation_guard emits warnings that distress claims must rest on contrasts not absolute levels, and reframes declared-impossibility as a competence signal; called in run_analysis (analyze.py:122) and written to report.
code_only_features.justification_quote: analyze.py:92 'Emit warnings so the writeup doesn't overclaim.'
